skill.name: readme-i18n
skill.description: Translate repository README files into localized variants while preserving Markdown structure, links, code blocks, badges, and language selectors.
skill.summary: Create multilingual README variants without breaking Markdown, links, anchors, or selectors.
skill.author: xixu-me

content.value_statement: README translation often breaks links, badges, code examples, and anchors. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create localized README variants while preserving repository mechanics.
actual_capabilities: Creates localized README sibling files using repository naming conventions.
Adds or updates one language selector across README variants.
Preserves Markdown tables, code fences, badges, URLs, and file paths.
Rewrites same-file anchor links after heading translation.
Uses glossary and do-not-translate terms when provided.
Reports created files, assumptions, and terms left unchanged.
limitations: Focused on README files, not full application internationalization.
Needs clear target languages or existing repository conventions.
Does not validate translations with native speakers.
Cannot guarantee links outside the repository remain available.

use_cases.title: Publish Multilingual README Files
use_cases.description: Create translated README variants that keep badges, links, code examples, and headings aligned with the source file.

use_cases.title: Standardize Documentation Language Switchers
use_cases.description: Add or update one language selector across README variants without duplicating selector blocks.

use_cases.title: Update Existing Localized Documentation
use_cases.description: Refresh localized README files after source changes while preserving prior naming patterns and unchanged technical tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Translate One README
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one target language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate README.md into Spanish. Create README.es.md. Preserve code blocks, badge URLs, commands, and file paths.

prompt_templates.title: Add Language Selector
prompt_templates.scenario: Add multiple languages and shared navigation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Chinese and Spanish README variants. Add one language selector near the top of each file.

prompt_templates.title: Extend Existing Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Repository already has one localized README.
prompt_templates.prompt: README.zh.md already exists. Add README.fr.md, update the selector in place, and keep existing naming conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize Changed Source
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare README.md with existing localized README files. Update only changed prose, then verify anchors, selectors, and code fence counts.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for Chinese and Spanish README variants.
output: Creates README.zh.md and README.es.md using the existing structure.
Adds one shared language selector to each README.
Notes preserved terms, links, badges, and assumptions.

output_examples.input: A repository already has README.zh.md and needs a French variant.
output: Creates the French README using the established naming pattern.
Updates the existing selector instead of adding another block.
Checks same-file anchors after translated headings are written.

output_examples.input: A source README changed after translations were published.
output: Compares the source with localized README files.
Updates changed prose without reformatting the full document.
Verifies code fence counts, links, and language selector consistency.

best_practices: Provide target languages and any glossary before localization starts.
Review translated headings and same-file anchors together.
Keep product names, package names, commands, and environment variables unchanged.
anti_patterns: Translating code fences, shell commands, URLs, or badge image sources.
Adding a second language selector instead of updating the existing one.
Changing section order without a repository reason.

faq.question: What files does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates localized README sibling files, such as README.es.md, when the repository uses that pattern.

faq.question: Can it update an existing language selector?
faq.answer: Yes. It updates an existing selector in place and avoids adding duplicate selector blocks.

faq.question: Does it translate code examples?
faq.answer: No. It preserves code fences, inline code, commands, flags, file paths, and environment variable names.

faq.question: How are same-file anchor links handled?
faq.answer: After headings are translated, same-file anchor links are rewritten to match the localized heading targets.

faq.question: What happens if target languages are unclear?
faq.answer: The skill checks repository conventions first. If the languages remain unclear, it asks the user once.

faq.question: Is this for full application localization?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on README and Markdown documentation localization workflows.
